Hi Priya,

Thanks for the discussion earlier — Mediconnect leadership flagged two outstanding items before procurement will sign the DPA: (1) a granular proof-of-processing map for EU-hosted workloads showing where data is processed/transited (we need to show onshore fallback and any multi-hop subprocessors), and (2) your position on key custody / escrow for onshore fallback in cases where we require UK-residency plus emergency support.

Concretely can you:  
- Share the current subprocessors CSV with processing locations and whether they are covered by SCCs/UK IDTA or an EU TIA fallback;
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept an HSM-backed key-escrow arrangement in a UK-vetted KMS for the subset of tokens tagged as EU-residency;
- Point us to a draft TIA scope if one exists (we're running legal and procurement in parallel).

Procurement would like these artifacts in the next 3 business days to keep the signature window this month.

Thanks,
Helen

Hi Helen — thanks, we can get these over. High-level answers first:

- Subprocessors: attaching an exported CSV that includes processing country, whether we have SCCs/UK IDTA coverage, and a short note on any multi-hop flows. See attachment: subprocessors-list.csv (stub).
- Key custody / escrow: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) integrations with major KMS providers. For an escrow arrangement we typically require either (a) an HSM-backed escrow managed by a mutually approved custodian, or (b) a split-escrow model where Redwood holds an operational key under strict access controls and the custodian holds a recovery share. We can run the exact wording by legal but the latter is our standard pattern for residency-backed emergency-support requests.
- TIA scope: attaching a draft TIA scope workbook with proposed controls and which processors it would cover: tia-scope-draft.xlsx (stub).

I'll loop in Kimberly to confirm any UK IDTA implications and Jordan for operational runbook / onshore fallback mechanics. If procurement wants a one-hour follow-up tomorrow, we can schedule.

Hi all — quick legal note on UK addendum / keys.

1) UK IDTA vs SCCs: For operators processing personal data originating in the EU, we map SCC coverage and UK IDTA coverage separately. If Mediconnect requires simultaneous compliance for both EU SCCs and a UK addendum for UK-origin data, we will: (a) include dual-mapping in the DPA (we've done this pattern before), and (b) make the TIA scope explicit about which datasets are covered by which instrument. That means we must label dataset IDs and processing routes in the proof-of-processing map you requested.

2) Key escrow: legal is comfortable with the split-escrow model Priya outlined, provided we: (a) define precise access criteria (emergency-only + two-person approval), (b) record all key retrieval events to an audit log with customer notification, and (c) place the custodian under a subprocessors appendix with contractual obligations. We will not accept a model that puts full custody outside contractual controls.

I've attached a redline snapshot of our DPA (redwood-dpa-v3-redlines.pdf) showing where the escrow and subprocessor language will live. We should also confirm whether Mediconnect procurement will accept a DocuSign cadence with separate signature for the UK addendum or one combined signature.

Kimberly
